headline: Gecko Robotics will supply its inspection robots and AI software to Anduril's new submarine-parts factories, the companies said.
score_reason: New on 8 Oct, confirmed by both firms; a supplier tie-in to a larger announcement from 6 Oct.
importance_line: Robotic inspection is being built into a US plan to make submarine parts faster, as industry misses the Navy's goal of two Virginia-class submarines a year; the shipyard is not yet permitted or built, and its first operations are not planned until 2030.
summary: Breaking Defense reports that Gecko, whose robots inspect the inside of metal structures such as welds, will test submarine components at Anduril's Orange County, California, site and at Arsenal-2, the Baltimore County shipyard that Anduril announced on Tuesday as a $6.6 billion investment, including up to $2.9 billion from the Navy. The shipyard is meant to start work in 2030, and it comes as industry has struggled to meet the Navy's goal of two Virginia-class submarines a year.
